problem: The lead says React turns JSX into real DOM elements, which skips a step. JSX first becomes React elements (plain objects), and ReactDOM turns those objects into DOM nodes. A careful student may think JSX is compiled straight to DOM APIs.
fix: React turns that JSX into plain objects called React elements, and ReactDOM renders those elements as real DOM nodes.

problem: "the browser shows Dosa2 items" reads like one run-together string and hides what is actually on screen. The student cannot tell whether the h2 and the p are separate elements.
fix: the browser shows a heading (h2) reading Dosa followed by a paragraph reading 2 items, both inside a div with class "card".

problem: Reactstrap is described as giving Bootstrap 4 components. Current Reactstrap versions target Bootstrap 5, so pinning the number invites a wrong answer in a viva.
fix: Reactstrap gives ready-made Bootstrap components such as <Button color="primary">; check which Bootstrap version your project installs.

problem: The clause "two siblings are two children of the component call" is muddled: there is no enclosing call, which is exactly why the transform fails with an adjacent-JSX-elements error. The fix given is right, but the explanation of the cause is unclear.
fix:
Adjacent JSX elements are a syntax error: the JSX transform must return a single element from the component, and two root elements cannot be wrapped into one call. Put them inside one parent,
...
, or a fragment <>....

problem: Suspense is credited with rendering parts of the tree on the server. Suspense shows fallback UI while code or data loads and lets the server stream the result; the rendering on the server is what Server Components do.
fix: React now has Server Components, which render parts of the tree on the server, and Suspense, which shows fallback UI while parts load and lets the server stream output to the browser.
